#### What this PR does / why we need it:
Related issue #127460

Utilize the `systemd watchdog` capability to restart the kubelet when the kubelet health check fails, and limit the maximum number of restarts within a given time period. This can enhance the reliability of the kubelet to some extent.

Example of  `systemd unit config`:

```
WatchdogSec=30s
Restart=on-failure
```

Feature Gate would be the best. I simply wasn't sure if we already have those read from config when we start the loop.

I think if we haven't parsed config yet, we probably shouldn't start the watchdog timer anyway.

But then, readers may be wondering, how do we handle failure during kubelet startup? Well, you'd code kubelet to [enable the watchdog and then immediately notify `READY=1`] once it is, eg, about to start admitting static Pods.

During startup, systemd can do something like watchdog wakeups, but you do that by notifying `EXTEND_TIMEOUT_USEC` (and a microsecond value) instead of `WATCHDOG`.

To make all of that protect your node and automate recovery, you would additionally:
- turn on a system level watchdog
- configure `TimeoutStartSec=` on the kubelet unit
- configure `TimeoutStartFailureMode=` on the kubelet unit

Once the watchdog integration graduates, we could send an initial watchdog notify even earlier. Even then, I'm inclined not to do that so that we can allow the kubelet side of this behavior to be configurable (future enhancements).

issue_context.title: integrate kubelet with the systemd watchdog
issue_context.body:
Implement the [systemd watchdog](https://0pointer.de/blog/projects/watchdog.html) in kubelet. Similar to https://github.com/containerd/containerd/issues/10329, we want to have a lightweight way to health check kubelet instead of requiring to run the health check process `curl`-ing the `/healthz` endpoint.

Implementation will require integrating with watchdog API, hooking those with the same checks that `/healthz` performs, and implement some e2e_node tests demonstrating this behavior. Documentation should be updated once implemented as well.

/sig node
/area kubelet
/kind feature

/good-first-issue
/help

For everybody who signed up to try it, this PR is going to the right direction: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/127566 but has some shortcomings. I commented on PR, listing here:

1. There should be no change of behavior when watchdog is not enabled (it is OK for 1 info message that it is not enabled, but NOT ok to report an error)
2. There should be no change of behavior on Windows. Do not even report that it is not enabled
3. When watchdog is enabled, but we failed to configure kubelet - kubelet should not start (e.g. time is not configured correctly)
4. The loop checks must be as lightweight as you can make them. Minimum allocations and no locks
5. Try to avoid false positives as much as possible.

PR should include code and unit tests. If you have a good idea on how to test e2e by emulating `daemon.Foo` behavior - it is an extra bonus.
